pilot: Al recovery — EW -> 1D-LTE -> NLTE ladder, executed
status: PILOT — the ABUNDANCE is verified; the gf GRADE is not. Not a ratified value; nothing written to any pool or reference.
selection_basis: lines chosen BEFORE any abundance was computed: unexplained stage-2 drop, zero contaminants above 10% of own depth, observed depth >= 2%, chi2 <= 0.01, REW below the -4.9 linear ceiling. Agreement with literature is corroboration, NEVER the criterion (validate-don't-tune).
corroboration: the Al_Amarsi2020_PySME NLTE grid contains EXACTLY two wavelengths, 6696.02 and 6698.67 — the two recovered lines and no others. The grid was built for these lines; the committed pool never carried either.

what_the_pool_holds_instead.note: both over-claim absorption (34.53 mA fitted vs 7.41 absorbed; and 119.95 mA across the 6696 pair vs 66.48 absorbed) and BOTH are rejected by the pipeline's own EW sanity filter when re-run — 5 lines in, 2 out, and the 2 it keeps are the recovered pair

STOP.detail: EW errors of 4.2% and 4.7% account for ~0.02-0.04 dex. The 0.339 dex line-to-line spread is NOT measurement noise. It is LARGER than the Mg 5528-vs-5711 discordance of 0.21 dex that keeps Mg owed, so Al faces the same question and must not be promoted on the mean alone.
STOP.likely_cause: relative gf. Both lines share EP 3.1427 and differ only in log gf (-1.886 vs -2.249), both ungraded (nist_grade absent, K75 provenance). A relative gf error maps directly onto the spread.
STOP.next_rung: synthesis (3 further Al candidates incl. 6696.020 deblend) + a graded Al gf pull

gf_caveat.what_i_got_wrong: I reported gf provenance from data/linelists/linelist_solar.csv (-1.886 / -2.249, the strongest HFS component) and warned the abundance might be overstated by 0.43-0.49 dex. That warning was unfounded: I quoted the wrong table.
gf_caveat.verified: RYA-353 single-sources gf for the live EW->abundance route. abundances_derive._build_ispec_line_regions calls apply_to_regions(), which overwrites every region's loggf from canonical_gf. Read back off the built linemasks directly: Al I 6696.0230 loggf -1.3470, Al I 6698.6730 loggf -1.6470 -- the canonical values.
gf_caveat.consequence: The pilot A(Al) values were computed on the adjudicated gf and STAND as computed.
gf_caveat.still_open: Both lines carry adjudication_status='pending' in canonical_gf with source VALD3 and no NIST grade. The VALUE is right for the gf we hold; whether that gf is right has never been decided.

gf_pull_blocked.evidence: HTTP 500 on every query including a control 'Fe I 5000-5010' minimal request; physics.nist.gov root returns 301, so the host is up and the CGI endpoint is failing. Error: "Can't use an undefined value as an ARRAY reference at ... lines1.pl line 701". Memory attributed this signature to bibrefs=1; it now fires without it, so the endpoint behaviour has changed since 2026-07-27.
gf_pull_blocked.repo_alternative: data/linelists/nist_reference.csv holds 40 graded rows and ZERO for Al. Al has never been graded in this repo.
gf_pull_blocked.known_primary: Kelleher & Podobedova 2008 JPCRD 37 p709 (Al/Si) -- already cited in canonical_gf for Al I 6696.185 at grade C+, so the source covers Al but was only ever applied to that one line.

single_source_finding.finding: linelist_solar.csv and canonical_gf.csv disagree on Al gf by a consistent -0.113 dex (HFS-summed linelist vs canonical, both lines).
single_source_finding.impact: NOT an abundance error -- the EW path reads canonical (RYA-353). It is a reporting hazard: any audit or plotting tool that reads linelist_solar for gf will state a different number than the one the pipeline used. I hit this myself twice today, in the RYA-707 promotion gate (repointed) and in the caveat above (retracted).
single_source_finding.rule: gf for reporting comes from canonical_gf, same as gf for computing. linelist_solar is not a gf source.
